5771.name: A Corner In the Salt Garden
5771.description: This area is somewhat sheltered from the wind by the castle walls, but there is no protection from what the wind carries. All around are benches and throne-like chairs, some wooden, some iron, and a few cut straight out of the headland rock. Dead ivy covers the walls here, rising from the shrubs below to the very top, every leaf still in place and every leaf white. The garden is entirely normal in all respects except that everything in it is cased in a fine crust of salt, as though a piece of somebody's warm country had been lifted out, dipped in the sea, and set down to dry. The flowers lean slightly in one direction, holding the shape of the gust that killed them. The whole scene makes for a rather ghastly paradox. The garden continues to the east and south, and an iron door is sunk into the north wall.

5752.name: Wandering Through the Salt Garden
5752.description: If it were not for the obvious abnormalities of the surroundings, it would be quite pleasant. But alas, the sheer strangeness of the garden cannot co-exist with comfort. A rigid bench made from bamboo sits sheltered under the bowed limb of a eucalyptus that in a warmer and drier place might be used by young lovers; here the bark comes away white on the hand. A patch of yellow orchids stands stopped in time in a small iron arbour to the left of the path, each petal stiff and slightly heavier than a petal should be. In between them a purple flower emerges, claiming dominion over the patch it did not outlive by much. What appears to be a tool shed lies to the south, and the garden continues to the east, west, and north.

5753.name: A Covered Gazebo Lost Among the Salted Flowers
5753.description: Framed in pine, this large gazebo provides strong shelter from the rain, but not the wind. Intertwined between the latticework and the roof is a long vine that wraps in and out of the crosshatching, circling the roof at least seven times. Every few feet along it a flower of a different species grows in solitude, each one sheathed in a delicate rind of salt. Accommodating benches line the outer edge, with a central round bench facing outward, dominating the middle of the structure. The crust covers the whole of the construction excepting the bench surfaces, which have been scraped clean to allow for use, and the floor, which has been swept. Exits lead to the south, east, and west.

5750.name: A Stopped Fountain In the Salt Garden
5750.description: Amidst the salted orchids and hibiscus, a fountain of beautiful marble construction stands with its water shut off. The design is simple: a round basin below and a long thin tower in the centre from which the water once fell in a circular curtain. The whole of it is furred white now, and the basin holds an inch of rain going green at the edges. Somebody has stopped maintaining the pump and has not stopped sweeping the path, which says something about the household. A collection of droppings on the flags beneath the fountain indicates that something still comes here to drink. A gazebo lies to the north, and the garden is visible to the east and west.

5697.name: The Northwestern Corner of the Grand Foyer
5697.description: A magnificent wall mural takes up the entire northern wall from top to bottom, and stretches across the foyer to the east. It depicts a drowned forest — a rain forest taken by the sea, its canopy standing out of green water and its floor gone. Gothic benches of iron and carved stone thrones lie throughout the scene, half swallowed. A sculpture of a young woman stands at the centre with something at her feet that the foliage hides. She is gazing up, past the castle walls, towards a point in the sky only she can identify. Off to the east, a small wooden gazebo can be seen amidst the leaves. To the south and the east the foyer continues, and to the west is a door accessing the west hall.

5695.name: The Northern End of the Grand Foyer
5695.description: The breathtaking mural against the north wall continues here. A hidden gazebo, sleeping among the thrush and leaves, lies overgrown with ivy and lichen. A small area surrounding it has been cleared, but only just enough to allow entrance and egress. The vines wind in and out of the latticework, showing how long it has stood. The thatch roof is starting to fray, and the painter has caught the moment before it goes. To the east and the west the foyer continues, and to the south a large fountain dominates the room.

5696.name: The Northeastern Corner of the Grand Foyer
5696.description: The giant mural on the wall to the north is visible from all parts of the foyer. Its grandeur is staggering up close, but far more impressive is the detail. The nests of absent birds rest in the branches, and in the few places where ground shows there are burrows and scattered underbrush. Footprints trample a path from the far right all the way through to the gazebo, just visible to the west. Over the footprints the painter has laid a thin wash of standing water, so that the whole scene reads as a place that has just been left. To the south and the west the foyer continues, and to the east is a door accessing the east hall.

5692.name: The Centre of the Grand Foyer
5692.description: A gigantic circular basin carved out of pale headland stone sits flush against the floor, forming the base of a fountain. Within it a hot, thick, blood-red liquid bubbles and steams as it swirls in a violent maelstrom, pouring away into an unseen drain. The pool is fed by a constant gush from a wound in one of the figures in the statue above. Of the two figures in the scene the female is far the more powerful sight: she stands well over six feet, built like a highlander, and stands over the fallen male wrenching her axe free of his sundered neck. The figures are cut from a blue-grey stone, in stark contrast to the gushing red. A chandelier hangs high above. The floor is a deep blue, dulled by the grim light, with strange white lines intersecting at all sorts of geometric angles — the sea-lanes of this coast, if you know how to read a chart. The cathedral ceiling rises all the way to the roof of the castle, starting lower at the sides and climbing to a domed zenith where the vile light resides. The grand foyer continues in all directions.

5679.name: The Southwestern Corner of the Grand Foyer
5679.description: Fancy wrought iron benches dominate this corner of the foyer, where the grey light starts to lose its power. The giant benches are covered in swirls and loops, with all manner of little demons and devils worked into the spires of the backrests. Painted a dark sea blue, they are a vulgar contrast with the rest of the dull scene. There appears to be a fountain in the centre of the foyer, but what form it takes is difficult to tell in this awful lighting. To the north and the east the foyer continues, and to the west is a door with a small barred window in it.

5693.name: The Southeastern Corner of the Grand Foyer
5693.description: The geometric white lines start to become sparser here in the corner of the foyer. Several wrought iron benches stand in the gothic style against the east and south walls, painted the same sea blue, standing out in the dim grey light. Portraits of several famous faces hang on the south wall above them, a testament to the people who have visited the castle — and, from the gaps and the paler rectangles between them, to the people who have stopped being mentioned. To the north and the west the foyer continues, and to the east is a door with a small barred window in it.

5710.name: The West Hall
5710.description: A twelve foot tapestry depicting a battle covers the northern wall, but the conflict displayed is not human. High on a sea stack, atop a small ledge, two adult sea-drakes begin their courtship. Legend has it the male must subdue the female by beating his wings against her to force her cooperation. She is quite resistant, and has got hold of his neck. Blood runs down his back and goes into the water below in threads. In the end the male will triumph, and the wound is only superficial; the resistance is there to convince him she will bear strong young. He is so confident that he has already dug out the nest ledge for the eggs, and its mouth is just below them. The hall runs east and west, while a door leads north.

5689.name: The Western End of the West Hall
5689.description: This hall is like the east hall, in that it shows the visual history of the castle and its army. Most of the images in this section are of a terrible battle at the edge of the world. The scene takes place in a sea-vale between two great stacks of rock, where winged drakes swoop down from the heights bearing fearless highlanders into bloody battle below. Empty suits of armour, placed on standing racks, elegantly serve as torch holders and give a sense of majesty to the hall. Each holds a torch in one hand and a flagstaff in the other. The ceiling is very high here, and banners hang down, leaving little room to swing a sword. The hall runs east and an iron door leads west while a wooden door leads north.

5707.name: The Southern End of the West Hall
5707.description: Branching off the guard's walk, this hall provides access to the ducal court, the Salt Garden, the Grand Foyer and the Barracks. It is vital to moving around this half of the castle. The floor is flat and smooth, cut from pieces of stone so large they must have been quarried from the headland itself, since there is no way they could have been carried far. The ambient light is pleasantly bright, and if the surrounding images were not so violent it might almost seem cheery. Empty suits of armour, placed on standing racks, elegantly serve as torch holders and give a sense of majesty to the hall. Each holds a torch in one hand and a flagstaff in the other. The ceiling is very high here, and banners hang down, leaving little room to swing a sword. The hall runs north and an iron door leads south.

5856.name: The Throne Room of the Ducal Court
5856.description: The stone here is bare and scrubbed, floor to ceiling, and colder than the rest of the castle for being so clean. A heavy throne rests against the centre of the back wall, spread with sealskins gone soft with use. It has broad furred armrests finished with the animals' own claws, and a matching footrest below. A great sea-drake's head is mounted above it as the headpiece, nearly the size of the throne itself, with fangs the length of a short sword and the salt of a hundred years still in its scales. A narrow red carpet leads from the pedestal at the south all the way up to the seat. Sprinkled along its length are what appear to be dried black orchid petals, brought a very long way to be dropped on a floor.

5699.name: The Northeastern Corner of the Ducal Court
5699.description: This is the court of the Duchess. At the north end sits her throne, where she spends very little time these days. The ceiling is higher than average, but not of cathedral proportions. Ambient light comes from a white-hot flame atop an onyx pedestal in the centre of the court. The floor is devoid of devices, unlike most of the castle. The walls, however, carry banners bearing the dragon's head of Draknor, smaller than the ones elsewhere and hung lower — it is apparent that this room is dedicated to somebody other than the house whose arms it flies. The court continues to the west and south. A door leads north, and an arched portal leads east to the West Hall.

5704.name: The Northwestern Corner of the Ducal Court
5704.description: The throne is not visible from this corner of the court, but the onyx pedestal shines with a darkness just to the east. Pillars of limestone support the ceiling, though they look more like decoration than structure, with carved textures and runic marks running up and down them like bark on a tree. The ceiling is stark white, peppered all over with tiny black spots. A draught rolls in from the north with the smell of the cold room behind that door in it. There is a door to the north, and the court continues to the east and south.

5703.name: A Malevolent Pedestal in the Ducal Court
5703.description: Evil emanates from this pedestal in waves so massive they are almost visible. A feeling of pure terror hangs in the air, proclaiming its presence with authority. The white-hot flame changes colour periodically, running from bright white through all the shades of grey and finally to black, holding each for only a second before it fades to the next. Nothing else is here, only the pedestal and the mesmerising flame.

5705.name: The Southwestern Corner of the Ducal Court
5705.description: This looks to be the most pleasant area of the court, as there are numerous chairs laid out row after row. They are comfortable-looking, but not too plush. The emblem sewn into the cushion of each backrest gives this away as the reserved section for the guard's upper echelon: the dragon's head with two crossed spears beneath it, unmistakable. Banners hang here listing the ranks of the elite squadron and their leader. The court continues to the east and north.

5702.name: The South End of the Ducal Court
5702.description: This is the main audience seating. Whenever visitors to the castle, or the household's non-enlisted, wish to address the Duchess, this is where they must come and wait. Permanent benches are affixed to the floor, seating perhaps thirty. Just past the onyx pedestal to the north the throne sits in its own room, patiently awaiting her. Even from this far away the white-hot flame is blindingly bright, and the shiny pale tiles lining the floor and walls do nothing to help the situation. To the east and west the court continues.

5701.name: The Southeastern Corner of the Ducal Court
5701.description: More comfortable, individual seating arrangements mark this as the section reserved for the hierarchy of the castle. Members of the clergy, the commander of the guard, the captain of the upper echelon and the Viscount are among the names embroidered on the cushions. A small bar sits south of the seating area, a permanent addition for use in large gatherings and, by the state of it, used at other times too. The throne is visible past the main seating to the north and west. The court continues to the west and north.
